# Sean McConoughey — public portfolio facts

Canonical page: https://smcconoughey.github.io/sean-mcconoughey-portfolio/
Updated: 2026-09-26

Sean McConoughey is an aerospace engineering B.S. student at Embry-Riddle Aeronautical University (expected 2028) and a test engineering intern at Saronic Technologies. His experience spans rocket ground control, liquid-engine development, industrial test engineering, instrumentation, and autonomous-system resilience. He is interested in future test, ground-systems, and launch-operations roles. Responsibility for human-spaceflight launch control is a long-term aspiration, not an experience claim or current title.

Documented work and status:
- ResistoJets Rocketry: founder and team captain. The team finished 17th of more than 800 in the American Rocketry Challenge, as documented by Embry-Riddle. The team won the 2024 NASA Student Launch Altitude Award, finishing 43 ft from a 3,900-ft target, as documented by Rutgers.
- Experimental Rocket Propulsion Lab (ERPL), Embry-Riddle: Sean developed ground-control software with telemetry, remote valve actuation, sequencing, and fault handling and served as ground controller for more than eight waterflow and liquid-engine static-fire tests. Embry-Riddle independently documents ERPL's 2025 Project Triton ethanol/LOX hot fires and Sean's ground-control and electronics roles. Project results belong to the team; detailed individual contribution is Sean's account.
- ERPL regenerative engine: as project lead, Sean rebuilt a Python analysis workflow connecting performance, heat transfer, injector sizing, and material strength. It enabled more than 1,000 design iterations and supported fabrication. This specific engine has not fired; it is distinct from the Project Triton engine that did.
- ERPL president: led work across technical programs, reviews, readiness, sponsors, and operations in a student lab of approximately 180 members.
- The Boring Company: test engineering intern, May–August 2026, working across mechanical systems, instrumentation, controls, computer vision, and field-test troubleshooting. Employer-specific designs and data are not published here.
- Saronic Technologies: current test engineering intern supporting autonomous maritime hardware; current design and test details are not published here.
- Embry-Riddle Center for Aerospace Resilient Systems (CARS): Sean implemented real-time analysis of noisy flight-simulator logs to return cyber-event cues to the simulated crew. The team demonstrated the simulator at DEF CON 33 Aerospace Village. Embry-Riddle documents Sean's contribution in its CARS internship article. Sean also worked on offline vulnerability analysis.
- Embry-Riddle Space Robotics and Generative Estimation Lab: research in GNSS-spoofing detection and autonomous-system fault monitoring.
